questions.who: An Israeli woman of about 50–65 who wants to look put-together, but not at the cost of comfort in the heat.
questions.everyday_problem: On hot days she has to choose between staying cool and looking put-together.
questions.current_workaround: She wears either a loose basic T-shirt, or a dressier blouse and puts up with the heat.
questions.why_frustrating: The basic tee is comfortable but makes her feel unfinished; the dressier blouse looks good in the mirror but feels heavy and clings by noon.
questions.what_changes: One light, breathable top whose cut glides softly over the body: cool and still put-together, from morning to evening.
questions.adina_observation: Every end of summer, women at the boutique counter say the same thing: 'It's hot, I want to be comfortable, but I don't want to look like I'm in house clothes.'
questions.core_belief: A woman shouldn't have to choose between staying cool and looking put-together.
questions.easiest_comparison: Loose basic tee (cool but shapeless) vs. dressy blouse (put-together but hot) vs. Payo (both).
questions.why_now: The official summer season ends, but the Israeli heat stays for weeks; end-of-season sale ₪359 → ₪179.

central_problem: In the heat, what keeps you cool looks sloppy, and what looks put-together feels heavy and clings.
customer_insight: She doesn't want 'comfortable clothes'; she wants to feel cool AND like herself — dressed, not in house clothes.

adina_belief: A woman shouldn't have to choose between staying cool and looking put-together.

why_now: End-of-season sale (₪359 → ₪179) while the heat is still here.
